gap: No result ChatGPT got states that VIOFO's "2K" rear camera on the A329S 3CH and Vantrue's "2.5K" rear camera on the N4 Pro S are the same thing: a 2560×1440 Sony STARVIS 2 IMX675 sensor at 30 fps. The rear cameras on the two picks are equal. The only spec difference among the channels is the cabin camera: VIOFO's is 2560×1440 with a 210° view, Vantrue's is 1920×1080.
standout_why: I compared against Gearsentials (cited), Product Bible (cited), Digital Camera World (cited) and DashCamTalk's best list (cited). Gearsentials lists the A329S rear as "2K30" and the N4 Pro S rear as "2.5K/1440p" but never says they match. Product Bible says Vantrue's "2.5K" rear is 1440p in the manual but doesn't set it against VIOFO's. Digital Camera World says the A329S front drops to 30 fps with the cabin camera on. DashCamTalk's list gives no rear pixel counts. None of them puts the two rear sensors side by side, and ChatGPT's own table ranked Vantrue's "2.5K" rear above VIOFO's "2K". So rivals have parts of the finding, but not the comparison.
decides: It backs the Vantrue N4 Pro S as the value pick. With all three channels recording, both cameras film the road ahead at 3840×2160 at 30 fps, and their rear cameras use the same 2560×1440 IMX675. VIOFO's higher price buys only two things here: a 2560×1440 cabin with a 210° fisheye and IR, and 60 fps at the front, which works only when the cabin camera is off. A shopper who needs the sharpest cabin view (rideshare drivers) has a reason to pay for VIOFO. Otherwise the N4 Pro S matches it on front and rear. The 70mai T800 is the only one of the three with a true 3840×2160 rear camera (IMX678), so it fits a shopper who cares most about the rear.

findings.label: Per-channel pixels, frame rate and sensor
findings.value: Front 3840×2160 at 30 fps (IMX678, 32 Mbps); cabin 1920×1080 at 30 fps (IMX662, 4 IR LEDs, 9.8 Mbps); rear 2560×1440 at 30 fps (IMX675, 14 Mbps)
findings.note: This makes Vantrue's "2.5K" rear the same pixel count and the same Sony IMX675 sensor as VIOFO's "2K" RC420. DashCamTalk lists parking mode as buffered, available with an optional hardwire kit. Gearsentials (cited by ChatGPT) gives the same per-channel figures for 3-channel mode: "4K front, 1080p cabin, and 2.5K/1440p rear at 30 frames per second".
